done_when: Close no longer runs the full test command on the laptop when the pull request's CI runs it: it runs fast_test when set, otherwise only the test files the change touched and the tests named after its changed source files; CI still runs the full suite and a red CI sends the item back. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body:
Close fails before review when a Go client changes a source file with a matching test.
Raise: Functional — Forge's unchanged `src/forge/init.py:58` sets a new Go repo's default command to `go test -v ./...`, with no `fast_test`. This branch appends selected filenames to that command, producing a command such as `go test -v ./... cart_test.go`. [Go's test command](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go) treats package patterns and file lists as different invocation modes, so this cannot run the selected test. The ruling about custom launchers needing `fast_test` does not cover this launcher: Forge ships it as the default. The named command test covers pytest, Vitest and Jest, but not Go.
findings.title: Not done: Close's default test selection breaks Go clients

findings.body:
Close cannot run selected Node tests on Windows once the repo has a few hundred test files.
Raise: Scale — This line adds one `--exclude` argument for every unselected Vitest file; lines 255–258 similarly put every unselected Jest path into one regex. With 200 test paths averaging 35 characters, the Vitest command exceeds [cmd.exe's 8,191-character limit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-US/troubleshoot/windows-client/shell-experience/command-line-string-limitation). `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` at line 269 then fails before the runner starts. The proof's Node cases use only four files, so they do not exercise this normal repo size.
findings.title: Close's Node test command exceeds the Windows shell limit in a realistic repo
